phrases.translation: Have We not uplifted your heart for you ˹O Prophet˺
phrases.text: God reminds His Prophet of His favours to him, to move him to gratitude and so to receive more. He says: have We not expanded your breast for you, O Muhammad, for guidance and faith and knowledge of the truth, so that your heart was softened and made a vessel for wisdom.
We forgave you the sins you had committed and removed from you the weight of the days of ignorance. In another reading it says We loosened from you the load that made your back crack.

phrases.translation: which weighed so heavily on your back
phrases.text: The commentators say the Prophet had committed sins that weighed on him, and God forgave them. Some say the burden was the association of partners he had known before he was sent. The image is a camel groaning under a load until it is worn out.

phrases.translation: and elevated your renown for you
phrases.text: God raised his renown, so that He is never mentioned without the Prophet being mentioned with Him, as in the testimony of faith. Qatada says it was raised in this world and the next, so that every preacher and every worshipper proclaims it.

phrases.translation: So, surely with hardship comes ease
phrases.text: Alongside the difficulty of the struggle against the idolaters there is hope and relief, in that you will be given the victory over them. The Prophet brought his companions good news with this verse and said that one hardship will never overcome two eases.
The second half repeats the first, so that the promise is doubled. Mujahid says the ease follows upon the hardship.

phrases.translation: So once you have fulfilled ˹your duty˺, strive ˹in devotion˺
phrases.text: The commentators differed. Some said: when you are free of the prayer, strive in supplication. Others said: when you are free of the struggle, strive in worship. Tabari takes the general sense: whenever you are free, occupy yourself with what brings you near to God.

phrases.translation: turning to your Lord ˹alone˺ with hope
phrases.text: Direct your longing to your Lord and to no other of His creatures, since the idolaters of your people had turned their needs to their gods and idols.
